diet.text: Small mammals, birds and eggs, reptiles and amphibians

overview.text: The Western (Northern Pacific) Rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper of western North America, from southern British Columbia to Baja California.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Size varies a lot between populations; mainland snakes often reach about 100 cm, and the record is 162.6 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern interior British Columbia in Canada, much of the western USA, and the Baja California Peninsula of Mexico.

diet.text: Finds prey with the heat-sensing pits on its face: birds, eggs, small mammals from mice to rabbits, and small reptiles and amphibians; young ones eat insects. Prey that runs off after the bite is tracked down once the venom works.

recognise.text: Heat-sensing pit between eye and nostril.
